text: The abdominal X-ray showing a "double bubble" sign is highly suggestive of duodenal atresia. To confirm this diagnosis and rule out other causes like malrotation or annular pancreas, please tell me if your baby has had any episodes of abdominal distension or if you noticed any failure to pass meconium within the first 48 hours.

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal Atresia. The clinical picture of bilious vomiting, the "double bubble" sign on X-ray, and the normal abdominal ultrasound are diagnostic. While the family history of pyloric stenosis is noted, the anatomical obstruction seen on imaging confirms duodenal atresia as the primary diagnosis.
